text:
Alex M: Kicking off a sizing thread for Dedicated clusters to serve llama-3-8b-int8. Need region/GPU comparisons (us-west1 / eu-west1 / ap-southeast1) and concrete concurrency targets + autoscale headroom. Who has the latest runs?
Jia Chen: I ran the cross-region benchmark last Wed. Uploaded charts to the bench bucket, short summary below. Full CSVs + plots: https://charts.internal/redwood/bench/175412 
Bench-Bot: chart upload complete: https://charts.internal/redwood/bench/175412/overview.png :white_check_mark:
Omar Ruiz: Quick digest (seq len 512, batch=8 where applicable, nf4 quant, greedy sampling):
- H100 (p4d-like): ~1200 tok/s per GPU sustain at concurrency=4, p50=28ms, p95=62ms.
- A100 40GB: ~820 tok/s per GPU at concurrency=3, p50=40ms, p95=95ms.
- L4: ~360 tok/s per GPU at concurrency=2, p50=95ms, p95=220ms.
Numbers vary slightly region->region (see below).
Priya Patel: For Dedicated sizing I recommend targeting ~60-70% sustained GPU utilization with autoscale-up at ~75% and scale-down when under ~50% for 5m window. That gives ~20-25% headroom for bursty queries and avoids backlog spikes.
Leo Ng: Translating to concurrency targets per GPU (for llama-3-8b-int8 workload): H100 -> 3 concurrent requests (avg tokens=200), A100 -> 2, L4 -> 1. Those produce p95 within SLA (~<120ms) on H100/A100, L4 is best-effort.
Alex M: Can you show the math for converting tok/s -> GPUs for a given qps? Need example for 10k qps (chat messages), assume avg 150 tokens per request.
Omar Ruiz: Sure — example calc: 10k qps * 150 tokens = 1.5M tok/s. If H100 gives 1200 tok/s, GPUs = ceil(1_500_000 / 1200) = 1250 GPUs. With 65% target util -> provision = ceil(1250 / 0.65) = 1924 GPUs. Autoscaler min/max and cost commit will adjust.
Priya Patel: For practical Dedicated clusters, we usually add a warm pool of ~10% of provisioned capacity (pre-warmed instances) and a fast-burst buffer (~5%) for short spikes. Also enable preemptive scale-up during marketing windows.
Jia Chen: Region notes — eu-west1 H100 numbers are ~5-8% lower in sustained tok/s due to slightly older drivers on the regional fleet; ap-southeast1 shows same per-GPU throughput but higher cold-start latencies when a new node is spun up.
Priya Patel: Kernel choices: On H100 enable fused attention + Triton custom kernels; that yields the 1200 tok/s. On A100 we used cuBLAS kernel paths with some Triton fwd kernels but saw lower perf. For L4 use the optimized L4 path (no fused attention) and expect larger p95 tails. Also prefer NF4 quant for quality/cost tradeoff here.
Alex M: Can you paste the autoscaler JSON snippet we recommend for Dedicated (scale policies + headroom)?
Jia Chen: Sure — example (pseudo):
```
autoscaler: {
  metric: gpu_utilization_p95,
  target: 0.65,
  scale_up_threshold: 0.75,
  scale_down_threshold: 0.5,
  cooldown_seconds: 300,
  warm_pool_percent: 10,
  burst_buffer_percent: 5
}
```
Use canary=true for rollouts so new nodes are warmed before traffic is routed.
SRE-Bot: Note: add lifecycle hook to run kernel warmup (2 short inference calls) on new nodes to avoid first-request penalty.
Omar Ruiz: One more practical: if customers want strict p95 < 100ms, lock them to H100 dedicated with pre-warmed nodes and limit concurrency per GPU to 3. A100 can meet p95~100-150ms depending on region and batching.
Leo Ng: For sales doc, recommended SKUs:
- H100 cluster: plan for 65% util target, include warm pool + 5% burst; price tier A.
- A100 cluster: plan for 60% util target, slightly higher node counts.
- L4 cluster: best-effort, only for low-cost dev/test.
Alex M: Great. Can someone produce a one-page table with GPUs->tok/s->recommended concurrency->provisioning factor (1/target_util) so sales/solutions can use it? cc @sales-team :eyes:
Priya Patel: I'll drop the table into the shared drive by EOD and include region multipliers. :thumbsup:
Jia Chen: Uploaded CSVs + per-region charts here: https://charts.internal/redwood/bench/175412/csvs.zip
Alex M: Thanks all — we'll use these numbers for the Dedicated sizing guidelines. Follow-ups if we need to run more quant modes (int8 asymmetric) or longer seq lengths.
